clue.text: Fair-minded people repulsed by such temper tantrums?

indicators.note: repulsed means pushed back, so the word for fair-minded people is turned round end to end

parts.note: good sports are people who play fair

explanation.surface: A wry question whether decent folk are put off by someone's tantrums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repulsed' turns SPORTS backwards; 'by such' points the solver at the answer itself as the thing reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A strop is British slang for a sulk or fit of bad temper, so plural tantrums fit.

clue.text: Tricky, hiding foreign cash in book

indicators.note: the book is hiding the cash, holding it within its covers
the cash sits in the book, confirming one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tome is a large book
roubles are the Russian currency

explanation.surface: Something awkward about money concealed inside a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Troublesome describes something causing difficulty, which is what tricky means as an adjective.

clue.text: Revealed shipping company's plan

parts.note: a secret that is out has been revealed
a line is a company running ships, as in a cruise line

explanation.surface: A shipping firm's scheme has been made public.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline is a rough plan or sketch of what is intended.

clue.text: German fellow beleaguered about end of working week

indicators.note: the word for beleaguered goes about, i.e. around, the day's abbreviation

parts.note: a beleaguered town is sieged, under siege
Friday, abbreviated Fri, ends the working week

explanation.surface: A German man is harassed as the working week finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Siegfried is a male German first name, the hero of Wagner's opera.

clue.text: Greek island hosts functions, producing warm feeling?

indicators.note: the island hosts, that is holds within it, the functions

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
sines are trigonometric functions

explanation.surface: A Greek island laying on events that leave visitors feeling warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosiness is a snug, comfortable warmth; the question mark admits the stretch from feeling to state.

clue.text: Officer unaccompanied through mountain pass

indicators.note: the lone word runs through the middle of the pass, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a col is a pass or saddle between peaks
lone means alone, unaccompanied

explanation.surface: An officer travelling alone over a mountain pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior army officer rank, above lieutenant colonel.

clue.text: Uses no words, presumably, to show authority

parts.note: one who uses no words says nothing; this gives the verb part
the nothing said is presumably nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: Silence as a way of asserting power.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, someone using no words 'says O', says nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's say-so is their authority or permission to do something.

clue.text: Rise of a right-winger leading new party? Impossible!

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the letters upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: Con is short for a Conservative
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A sceptic dismissing a right-winger heading a new party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise of' turns the first two pieces upwards to give NOCA, and 'leading' puts that in front of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal refusal meaning it cannot be done, an exclamation of impossibility.

clue.text: Drunkard outstretched initially in middle of street

indicators.note: the letter is placed in the middle of the street's abbreviation
initially picks out the first letter of outstretched

explanation.surface: A drunk sprawled out in the middle of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A sot is an old word for a habitual drunk.

clue.text: Heard pop duo's low-key publicity?

indicators.note: heard signals that the band's name is spoken and the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: Soft Cell were the British synth-pop duo behind Tainted Love

explanation.surface: Listening to a pop duo's understated promotional campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft sell is gentle, persuasive selling or advertising rather than a hard push.

clue.text: Holiday going about round Switzerland? Not in these!

definitions.text: Holiday going about round Switzerland? Not in these!

indicators.note: the reversed holiday word goes round the country code
going about means turning to face the other way, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a stay is a holiday visit
CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A tour around Switzerland, and the craft you couldn't use for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going about' gives YATS. Switzerland is landlocked, so a sea-going holiday there is out, which is the whole clue's point.
explanation.definitionFit: Yachts are sailing boats used for cruising holidays, useless in a country without coastline.

clue.text: Nice fee R Burton negotiated for film

indicators.note: terms that are negotiated are worked over and rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Agreeing a good fee for the actor Richard Burton to appear in a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief Encounter is the 1945 David Lean romantic movie with Celia Johnson and Trevor Howard.

clue.text: Northern bird in friendly environment? Right

indicators.note: the northern bird sits in the environment word

parts.note: being in one's element means being in a congenial setting
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A northern bird at home in pleasant surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: An entitlement is a right to have or do something.

clue.text: Phone engineers at first making things better?

indicators.note: the engineers come at first, before the phone word

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
to dial is to phone

explanation.surface: Calling in the engineers first to put things right.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial means intended to correct or improve something.

clue.text: Translation of Breton author

indicators.note: a translation changes a text's form, so these letters are moved into another order

explanation.surface: A version of a book in the Breton language.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brontë sisters, Charlotte, Emily and Anne, were famous Victorian novelists.

clue.text: Heckler's noise cut short in pub, meeting resistance

indicators.note: the shortened noise goes in between the pub and the resistance letter
the pub meets, sits next to, the resistance letter

parts.note: a bar is a pub
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: cut short means the noise word loses its last letter

parts.note: a racket is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A rowdy heckler making a din in a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A barracker is someone who jeers or shouts down a speaker; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Developed make of car to accommodate setter

indicators.note: the car make makes room for the setter inside it

parts.note: Ford is a car manufacturer
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A car firm giving the crossword compiler a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: Formed means shaped or brought into being, i.e. developed.

clue.text: Name on bottom of large tent

indicators.note: in a down clue the name sits on top of the following letter

parts.note: a marque is a brand name, especially of cars

indicators.note: the bottom of a down word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A name printed at the foot of a big tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquee is a large tent used for parties or shows.

clue.text: I'm a Tory, confused about Liberal's awareness of what's right?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the Liberal letter
confused means mixed up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A muddled Conservative pondering a Liberal's sense of ethics.
explanation.definitionFit: Morality is the sense of principles distinguishing right from wrong.

clue.text: Fellow troubled by European sea creature

indicators.note: the European letter is placed by, next to, what comes before

parts.note: a man is a fellow
ate, as in what's eating you, means troubled

explanation.surface: A man bothered by someone from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The manatee, or sea cow, is a large plant-eating marine mammal.

clue.text: Knocked unconscious, oaf receives help

indicators.note: the oaf receives, takes in, the help

parts.note: a lout is an oaf
aid is help

explanation.surface: A thug, flattened, being given first aid.
explanation.definitionFit: To be laid out is to be knocked flat, senseless.

clue.text: Typical salesman

definitions.meaning: an adjective: serving as an example of its class
a sales rep, travelling for a firm

explanation.surface: Just what you'd expect from a salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both characteristic of a group and an agent selling for a company.

clue.text: Sacred writings, in part useful when read up

indicators.note: read up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, backwards
in signals the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Holy texts that are partly useful when studied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks ARTUS from pART USeful; 'when read up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutras are Hindu or Buddhist scriptures, aphorisms of sacred teaching.

clue.text: Free to leave after middle section of race

indicators.note: the leave word comes after the middle letters
the middle section means the central letters of race

parts.note: to quit is to leave

explanation.surface: Allowed to go once half the race is run.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquit is to clear and release someone of a charge.

clue.text: Fellow's not finished cuppa

indicators.note: not finished means the fellow word loses its last letter

parts.note: a chap is a fellow; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A man who hasn't finished his cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha (char) is British slang for tea, as is cuppa.

clue.text: Assume responsibility and head for safety, avoiding cold

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving out, so the cold letter is dropped

parts.note: to take cover is to head for safety

explanation.surface: Taking charge and getting to shelter while dodging the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To take over is to assume control or charge of something.

clue.text: Refurbished fleapit doesn't show it with fantastic Bob Hope film

indicators.note: a refurbished building is redone, so the letters are rearranged
the letters of it are not shown, removed from the mix

parts.note: ace means excellent, fantastic

explanation.surface: A smartened-up fleapit cinema refusing to screen a great Bob Hope film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refurbished' with 'doesn't show it' leaves the letters PALEF. A fleapit is British slang for a shabby old cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paleface is a 1948 Western comedy starring Bob Hope and Jane Russell.

clue.text: Take a spin round London gallery by middle of afternoon

indicators.note: the middle of afternoon is its central letter

parts.note: O is round in shape
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A spin round a London gallery in mid-afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn or spin about an axis.
